basis: Absent menstruation is a reproductive disorder; an endocrine cause is not inherent to this umbrella concept.
Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy; pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/2 and myopathy/weakness in 1/2. Neurologic involvement also reported; omitted under the four-axis cap.
Inherited platelet aggregation failure. Mucosal bleeding and bruising do not establish local organ damage; intracranial hemorrhage is uncommon despite the isolated case annotation.
Splenic tissue necrosis caused by interrupted arterial or venous circulation; both the spleen and its vascular supply define the disease.
A neurodevelopmental disorder defined by impaired social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors.
Skeletal dysplasia and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome. Retinal detachment is reported, but its frequency and status as a major criterion are unclear.
Defined by abnormal pupillary light responses with preserved accommodation; an underlying infection or broader neurologic disease is not intrinsic to this concept.
A purely psychiatric paraphilic disorder without intrinsic damage to any listed organ axis.
Short ribs and skeletal malformations define the group; pulmonary hypoplasia from thoracic constriction is common (approximately >=30%). Renal/hepatic involvement varies by subtype.
Open spinal dysraphism combines split spinal cord and exposed malformed neural tissue, with the vertebral closure defect of spina bifida aperta.
Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle. Cardiac disease and intrinsic pulmonary damage are not established as common across this heterogeneous umbrella.
Limb and vertebral malformations define the syndrome; duodenal atresia occurs in 80-99%, and thymic aplasia affecting immune development in 30-79%.
Isolated parathyroid hormone deficiency causes hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia. Hypocalcemic seizures do not establish lasting neurologic injury.
Carcinoma originates in scrotal skin epithelium; its subtypes include cutaneous squamous cell, basal cell and Paget carcinomas.
Defective airway ciliary clearance causes chronic respiratory disease; middle-ear clearance dysfunction with recurrent otitis occurs in 2/5 (40%). Situs inversus alone is not cardiac damage.
Mammary carcinoma involving the nipple-areola complex; breast and nipple disease fall outside the listed organ axes.
Muscle phosphorylase kinase deficiency is a glycogen metabolic myopathy with progressive weakness, abnormal muscle glycogen and muscle fiber injury.
Isolated congenital horizontal pendular nystagmus impairs ocular motor function; no additional neurologic disorder is established.
Epidermolytic ichthyosis causes scaling, blistering, erosions and palmoplantar keratoderma; manifestations are confined to skin.
Callosal agenesis and developmental impairment, congenital cardiac defects and ocular abnormalities define the syndrome. Genital malformations have no axis.
Developmental epileptic encephalopathy; atrial septal defect and aortic regurgitation each occur in 1/3 (~33%) reported patients, although the cohort is small.
PRPF31-related retinal degeneration causes rod-cone dysfunction, night blindness and progressive visual loss.
Premature cranial suture fusion with structural abnormalities of the cranial base and digits defines a skeletal malformation syndrome.
Angular blepharoconjunctivitis is typically bacterial, classically associated with Moraxella, affecting the conjunctiva and eyelid canthi.
Clonorchis infection directly occupies and inflames the biliary passages, which belong to the hepatic axis; later cholangiocarcinoma is a separate disease.
